what_happened: The person running Athena used a wait command to hold until the running batch ended. The command checked for a running process by name, but the command's own text contained that name, so the check matched itself and never saw the batch end. The helper script it depended on was also never written. Because of this, the approved home page job and the next batch did not start, and Athena sat idle for about an hour. No work was judged bad.
cause: Athena gives the person running Athena no built-in way to wait for a drain or batch to end and then start the next work. Waiting is done with ad hoc shell commands, and nothing shows whether such a command is waiting on the right thing. A name-based process check can match the command that runs it. Nothing reports when the queue has approved work but nothing is running. Safe use depends on the person running Athena remembering the pitfall, as in the other hand-command mistakes where Athena does not guard the person's view of state.
prevention: Add a first-class Athena command, such as `athena wait-drain [--then <command>]`, that waits on the drain's recorded run state (a pid or lock file Athena owns), not on a process name. Pair it with an idle alert: if approved or queued work exists and no drain has run for a set time, `athena status` flags it and a notice is sent. Until then, the default is to check by exact installed-binary path or recorded pid, and to write helper scripts to a file before running them.
proposed_request: Add an `athena wait-drain` command that blocks until the current drain ends, using the drain's recorded pid or lock state rather than a process-name search. It should accept an optional follow-on command to run, such as starting the next drain. Exit non-zero if no drain is running, and print what it is waiting on. Also make `athena status` show an idle warning when approved or queued items exist, no drain is running, and the last drain ended more than 15 minutes ago. Acceptance: a test starts a fake drain, runs wait-drain, and shows it returns only after the drain ends; a test shows a command line containing the word 'athena' does not satisfy the wait; a test shows the idle warning appears for queued work with no running drain and is absent while a drain runs.
